exercises.name: B-Skip
instructions: Stand tall with the chest up and eyes forward.
Skip off one foot while lifting the opposite knee to hip height, as in an A-skip.
Extend the lifted leg forward, then sweep it down and back so the foot lands under the hips.
Alternate legs and travel forward for 20 to 30 metres with relaxed, opposite arm swing.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back as the leg extends, or kicking straight out from the floor without lifting the knee first.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk through the pattern as a march before adding the skip.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It rehearses pulling the foot back under the body, which is the answer to overstriding.

exercises.name: Ankling Drill
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Take very short steps forward, rolling each foot down from the toe so the heel barely touches the ground.
Keep the knees low and the steps quick and springy.
Learn the pattern slowly, then raise the step rate over 10 to 20 metres.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the knees high, or letting the heels drop heavily on each step.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it at walking speed until the foot action feels smooth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the foot and ankle to load and release quickly, which every running step needs.

exercises.name: Strides
instructions: After an easy run, find a flat stretch of roughly 80 to 100 metres.
Build speed smoothly over the first third until you are running fast but relaxed, well short of an all-out sprint.
Hold that speed with tall posture and quick steps, then ease down gradually.
Walk or jog easily for 60 to 90 seconds and repeat 4 to 8 times.
exercises.commonMistakes: Turning them into flat-out sprints, or reaching the foot out in front to lengthen the step.
exercises.beginnerModification: Run 4 shorter strides at a comfortably quick pace with a full walk back.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A few short accelerations keep fast running mechanics sharp without adding fatigue.

exercises.name: Hill Repeats
instructions: Warm up with at least 10 minutes of easy running and find a steady hill.
Run up the hill at a hard, controlled effort, judging it by feel rather than pace.
Keep the steps short and the trunk tall, with a slight lean from the ankles.
Jog or walk slowly back down to recover, then repeat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sprinting the first repeat and fading on the rest, or bending at the waist as the hill bites.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a gentle slope, shorten each effort to 30 seconds and walk down.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Hills build running strength and fitness at lower speed and lower impact than flat sprints.

exercises.name: Tempo Run
instructions: Jog easily for 10 minutes to warm up.
Raise the pace to comfortably hard, an effort where you can say a few words but not hold a conversation.
Hold that effort evenly for 20 to 30 minutes.
Finish with 5 to 10 minutes of easy jogging.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting too fast and slowing through the second half, or running it like a race.
exercises.beginnerModification: Split the hard running into blocks of 5 to 10 minutes with 2 minutes of easy jogging between them.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Sustained work near threshold raises the pace you can hold before fatigue builds.

exercises.name: Fartlek Run
instructions: Warm up with 10 minutes of easy running.
Pick a landmark or a time and run faster until you reach it.
Drop back to an easy jog until your breathing settles.
Keep mixing faster and easier stretches of different lengths by feel, then cool down with easy running.
exercises.commonMistakes: Making every surge an all-out sprint, or stopping to walk instead of jogging between efforts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Alternate 1 minute a little quicker with 2 minutes very easy.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Unstructured pace changes train you to shift speed and recover while still moving.

exercises.name: Long Slow Run
instructions: Plan a route or time that is longer than any other run in your week.
Start at an easy pace where you can talk in full sentences.
Hold that easy effort the whole way and let pace drop on hills.
Finish feeling you could have continued, then walk for a few minutes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Running it at a medium-hard effort, or extending the distance by a big jump from one week to the next.
exercises.beginnerModification: Add walk breaks every few minutes and keep the total time modest.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Time on feet at low intensity builds the aerobic base everything else sits on.

exercises.name: Cadence Drill
instructions: During an easy run, count your steps for one minute to find your usual step rate.
Set a metronome about 5 percent faster than that number.
Run for 1 minute matching your steps to the beat, keeping the same speed by taking shorter, lighter steps.
Jog normally for 1 to 2 minutes and repeat several times.
exercises.commonMistakes: Speeding up instead of shortening the step, or jumping to a much higher rate in one go.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the faster rhythm for 30 seconds at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A slightly quicker step rate shortens the stride and softens each landing.

exercises.name: Easy Recovery Run
instructions: Start at a gentle jog, slower than feels necessary.
Keep the effort low enough to breathe through the nose or talk freely.
Stay relaxed and tall with short, light steps for about 20 to 30 minutes.
Take a walk break if your form starts to get heavy or sloppy.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the pace creep up into a moderate run, which turns a recovery day into another training day.
exercises.beginnerModification: Alternate a few minutes of jogging with a minute of walking.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Gentle running between hard days keeps the habit and the blood flow without adding stress.

exercises.name: Run-Walk Intervals
instructions: Walk briskly for 5 minutes to warm up.
Run at an easy pace for 1 minute.
Walk for 4 minutes to recover.
Repeat the run and walk four times, then walk for 5 minutes to cool down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Running the minute too fast, or adding running time before the current session feels comfortable.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the run to 30 seconds and keep the walks the same.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Walk breaks let you build up to running a little at a time instead of all at once.

exercises.name: Track Repeats
instructions: Warm up with 10 to 15 minutes of easy running and a few strides.
Run a set distance, such as 400 metres, at a hard pace you can repeat.
Jog or walk for about as long as the hard effort took.
Repeat for the planned number of efforts, aiming for the same time on each, then cool down.
exercises.formCue: Same pace, first rep to last.
exercises.commonMistakes: Running the first repeats too fast and falling apart, or cutting the recovery short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Halve the distance of each repeat and walk the full recovery.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Hard, measured efforts with planned rest let you spend more total time near top aerobic effort.

exercises.name: Incline Treadmill Walk
instructions: Start the belt flat at a comfortable walk for a few minutes.
Raise the incline to a moderate grade and set a speed you can hold without gripping the rails.
Walk tall with the arms swinging freely and the whole foot pushing through each step.
Lower the incline and walk flat for a few minutes to finish.
exercises.commonMistakes: Holding the handles and leaning back, which takes the work away from the legs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lower incline and slower speed, and rest a hand lightly on the rail only for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The grade raises the heart rate and works the hips hard at walking speed.

exercises.name: Elliptical Trainer
instructions: Step onto the pedals, hold the moving handles and start striding at a low resistance.
Stand upright with the shoulders over the hips.
Push and pull the handles in time with the legs so the stride feels like a smooth run.
Raise the resistance until the effort matches the session, and slow gradually before stepping off.
exercises.commonMistakes: Slouching over the console, or letting momentum carry the pedals at a resistance that is too low.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the fixed handles and keep the resistance light for short sessions.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives a running-style effort for arms and legs with very little impact.

exercises.name: Stair Climber
instructions: Step on, start at a slow speed and find a steady rhythm.
Stand upright with the hands resting lightly on the rails for balance only.
Place the whole foot on each step and lift the feet clear as the steps turn.
Raise the speed gradually and build the length of the session over several weeks.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning heavily on the rails or hunching over them, which takes load off the legs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a slow speed for a few minutes at a time with flat walking between bouts.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Steady climbing is demanding cardio that also builds hip and thigh endurance.

exercises.name: Power Walk
instructions: Stand tall with the eyes on the horizon, chest lifted and midsection lightly braced.
Bend the elbows to roughly a right angle and swing the arms forward and back from the shoulders.
Land on the heel and roll through to push off the toes.
Pick up speed by taking quicker steps rather than longer ones.
exercises.commonMistakes: Overreaching with the front foot, or looking down and rounding the shoulders.
exercises.beginnerModification: Alternate a few minutes of brisk walking with a few minutes at a normal pace.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Brisk walking with good form is cardio almost anyone can do daily and recover from.
